sources.entry: Zero-TOTP - Complete, reliable, secure and zero-trust webapp based on zero-knowledge encryption to store your TOTP codes. (Source Code) GPL-3.0 Docker

summary.one_liner: Zero-TOTP is a zero-knowledge encrypted TOTP code manager offered as a web app, iOS app and CLI app, with a self-hostable web app.
summary.what_it_does: Zero-TOTP stores your TOTP codes in an vault that is encrypted locally with a passphrase before upload, so the hosting provider cannot read the data. The vault can be kept in the zero-totp.com database (default), in Google Drive with auto-sync, or on your own machine. The vault can be opened from the zero-totp.com web app, the iOS app, the CLI app, a rescue frontend at rescue.zero-totp.com that lets you upload and decrypt a vault, or a self-hosted instance via a Docker image. The web app can be self-hosted by deploying a few containers, following the project documentation. The README describes the project as 100% open source and invites merge requests.
use_cases: access 2FA codes from phone or browser
back up TOTP secrets to Google Drive or a local file
recover TOTP codes if the main service is down
manage 2FA codes from the command line
how_to_run: Self-host the web app by following the instructions in the project documentation (deploys a few containers)
Use the zero-totp Docker image to run a local instance
notable: Zero-knowledge encryption: data is encrypted locally with a passphrase before upload
Vault can be stored in the hosted database, Google Drive (auto-sync), or on your own machine
Five independent access platforms including a static rescue frontend hosted on GitHub Pages
Available as web app, iOS app and CLI app
caveats: iOS app and CLI app are not yet stable according to the README progress table (CLI is in development only; iOS is in development)
Self-hosting requires deploying multiple containers per the documentation
Images and icons are free to use but not for commercial purposes
